bib.title: LLaMA: Open and Efficient Foundation Language Models

question: Can models trained only on publicly available data, for longer than compute-optimal, reach state-of-the-art quality at small sizes that are cheap to serve?
hypothesis: For a target performance, a smaller model trained on more tokens is cheaper at inference than a larger compute-optimal one.
contributions: LLaMA, a collection of foundation models from 7B to 65B parameters trained on 1T-1.4T tokens
Training on publicly available data only
Release of all models to the research community
Benchmarks on 20 tasks plus bias, toxicity and carbon footprint analysis

method.summary: Decoder-only transformers (7B, 13B, 33B, 65B) with pre-RMSNorm, SwiGLU and rotary embeddings, pretrained on a 1.4T-token mix of public sources (CommonCrawl, C4, GitHub, Wikipedia, Books, ArXiv, StackExchange) with AdamW and a cosine schedule. Evaluated zero-shot and few-shot on 20 benchmarks against GPT-3, Gopher, Chinchilla, PaLM, OPT and others; one instruction-finetuned variant (LLaMA-I) is tried on MMLU.

datasets.name: English CommonCrawl
datasets.preprocessing: CCNet: line-level dedup, fastText language ID, n-gram LM quality filter; plus a linear classifier keeping Wikipedia-reference-like pages

datasets.name: C4

datasets.name: Github
datasets.source: Google BigQuery public GitHub, Apache/BSD/MIT licences only
datasets.preprocessing: line-length and alphanumeric heuristics, boilerplate removed by regex, file-level exact dedup

datasets.name: Wikipedia
datasets.preprocessing: hyperlinks, comments and formatting boilerplate removed

datasets.name: Books (Gutenberg and Books3)
datasets.source: Project Gutenberg; Books3 from The Pile
datasets.preprocessing: book-level dedup, books with more than 90% overlap removed

datasets.name: ArXiv
datasets.preprocessing: text before first section and bibliography removed, comments removed, macros inline-expanded

datasets.name: StackExchange
datasets.preprocessing: HTML stripped, answers sorted by score

training.objective: next-token prediction (standard language modelling; inferred from the training-loss curve and 'standard optimizer')
training.lr_schedule: cosine, final learning rate 10% of maximal
training.epochs: about 1 epoch for most data; about two epochs on Wikipedia and Books (Table 1: 1.10 CommonCrawl, 1.06 C4, 0.64 Github, 2.45 Wikipedia, 2.23 Books, 1.06 ArXiv, 1.03 StackExchange, at 1.4T tokens)
training.compute: 65B: 1,022,362 GPU-hours, 449 MWh, 173 tCO2eq; 7B 82,432 GPU-h; 13B 135,168; 33B 530,432 (Table 15). Whole development about 2048 A100-80GB for approximately 5 months, 2,638 MWh, 1,015 tCO2eq

other.throughput: around 380 tokens/sec/GPU on 2048 A100 GPU with 80GB for 65B
other.efficiency: xformers causal attention that skips masked scores and does not store attention weights; manual backward for transformer layers to save expensive activations; model and sequence parallelism; overlap of compute and all_reduce communication
other.positional: rotary embeddings at each layer, no absolute positions

inference.decoding: NaturalQuestions/TriviaQA: greedy, answer cut at first line break, final dot or comma; RealToxicityPrompts: greedy; code: sampling
inference.temperature: 0.1 for pass@1, 0.8 for pass@100 and pass@80
inference.samples: MATH maj1@k with k=256, GSM8k k=100 (Minerva 540B uses k=64 and 40); pass@k estimated as in Chen et al. 2021
inference.prompting: zero-shot: task description plus test example; few-shot: 1 to 64 examples. HumanEval zero-shot, MBPP 3-shot, MMLU 5-shot. QA prompt prefix 'Answer these questions:\n'

other.multiple_choice_scoring: completion with highest likelihood normalised by characters (Gao et al. 2021); for OpenBookQA and BoolQ, P(completion|context)/P(completion|'Answer:')

metrics.name: Exact match (NaturalQuestions, TriviaQA)

eval.protocol: Single run per model; no seeds or significance tests stated. Baseline numbers are taken from the corresponding papers (some read from figures). TriviaQA uses the filtered dev set (baselines used the unfiltered test set); NaturalQuestions uses the 3610-question open-domain test split.

limits: Evaluation ignores held-out contamination analysis; none is reported.
Baseline numbers come from other papers with different evaluation sets (TriviaQA filtered dev vs unfiltered test) and some are read from figures, so comparisons are indicative.
Toxicity scores come from a third-party API the authors do not control, so comparison with prior work is difficult.
Authors concede bias and toxicity benchmarks are not sufficient to understand the risks; model likely hallucinates (TruthfulQA).
Instruction finetuning is a single experiment on MMLU only; the finetuning data and hyperparameters are not given.
No ablations of the architecture changes or the data mix; no sequence length, vocabulary size or precision stated.
Training-cost claims: 65B ran 1.4T tokens for 21 days; smaller models trained 1.0T tokens, so size comparisons confound parameters and tokens.
Dated: results predate later LLaMA releases and instruction-tuned open models; MMLU 5-shot gap to PaLM-540B and Chinchilla.
